citation.title: ShellCheck: README, shellcheck(1) manual and wiki (SC2086, SC2164, SC2046, SC2155)

claims.planned: ShellCheck is a static analysis tool for sh/bash scripts
claims.finding: README title: 'ShellCheck - A shell script static analysis tool'; man page: 'a static analysis and linting tool for sh/bash scripts'. GPLv3, written in Haskell. Dialects selectable with -s: sh, bash, dash, ksh, busybox; default is deduced from a `# shellcheck shell=` directive, then the shebang, then the file extension. `sh` means POSIX sh, 'not the system's'.
claims.quote: ShellCheck is a static analysis and linting tool for sh/bash scripts. It's mainly focused on handling typical beginner and intermediate level syntax errors and pitfalls where the shell just gives a cryptic error message or strange behavior

claims.planned: SC2086 (double quote to prevent globbing and word splitting) wording; SC2164 (cd … || exit); SC2046; SC2155
claims.finding: Exact wiki titles: SC2086 'Double quote to prevent globbing and word splitting.' | SC2164 'Use `cd ... || exit` in case `cd` fails.' | SC2046 'Quote this to prevent word splitting.' | SC2155 'Declare and assign separately to avoid masking return values.' Severities as emitted by 0.9.0: SC2086 info (shown as 'note' in gcc format), the other three warning. The message text printed by the tool for SC2164 is slightly longer than the wiki title: "Use 'cd ... || exit' or 'cd ... || return' in case cd fails."
claims.quote: Quoting variables prevents word splitting and glob expansion, and prevents the script from breaking when input contains spaces, line feeds, glob characters and such.

extra_findings.quote: It's actually "Split the first argument by IFS (spaces, tabs and line feeds). Expand each of them as if it was a glob. Join all the resulting strings and filenames with spaces. Print the result."

extra_findings.fact: SC2164 rationale: a failed cd means the rest of the script runs in the wrong directory.
extra_findings.quote: If/when it does, the script will keep going and do all its operations in the wrong directory. This can be messy, especially if the operations involve creating or deleting a lot of files.

extra_findings.fact: SC2164 is suppressed by any `set -e` in the script, 'even though it won't necessarily prevent the issue'.
extra_findings.quote: Having a `set -e` command anywhere in the script will disable this message, even though it won't necessarily prevent the issue.

extra_findings.fact: SC2046: fix by quoting the command substitution, not the data; legitimate exception is e.g. `gcc $(pkg-config --libs openssl)`.
extra_findings.quote: When command expansions are unquoted, word splitting and globbing will occur. This often manifests itself by breaking when filenames contain spaces.

extra_findings.fact: SC2155: `export foo="$(mycmd)"` / `local foo=$(mycmd)` discard mycmd's exit status, defeating conditionals, set -e and traps.
extra_findings.quote: In the original code, the return value of `mycmd` is ignored, and `export` will instead always return true. This may prevent conditionals, `set -e` and traps from working correctly.

$ f() { local foo=$(false) && echo "error was hidden"; }; f
error was hidden

extra_findings.fact: Exit codes: 0 no issues, 1 some issues, 2 some files could not be processed, 3 bad syntax (unknown flag), 4 bad options (unknown formatter) — usable directly in CI.
extra_findings.quote: 0: All files successfully scanned with no issues. 1: All files successfully scanned with some issues. 2: Some files could not be processed (e.g. file not found). 3: ShellCheck was invoked with bad syntax (e.g. unknown flag). 4: ShellCheck was invoked with bad options (e.g. unknown formatter).

extra_findings.fact: Suppress one finding with a directive comment on the line before.
Install on Debian/Ubuntu: `sudo apt install shellcheck` (README). Ubuntu 24.04's package is version 0.9.0. Web version at shellcheck.net tracks the latest commit.
Actual output on a five-line bad script (cd with no guard; rm -rf $1/*; ls -l $(find ...); local out=$(mycmd); export v="$(other)").
extra_findings.quote:
/tmp/bad.sh:2:1: warning: Use 'cd ... || exit' or 'cd ... || return' in case cd fails. [SC2164]
/tmp/bad.sh:3:8: warning: Use "${var:?}" to ensure this never expands to /* . [SC2115]
/tmp/bad.sh:3:8: note: Double quote to prevent globbing and word splitting. [SC2086]
/tmp/bad.sh:4:7: warning: Quote this to prevent word splitting. [SC2046]
/tmp/bad.sh:5:13: warning: out appears unused. Verify use (or export if used externally). [SC2034]
/tmp/bad.sh:5:13: warning: Declare and assign separately to avoid masking return values. [SC2155]
/tmp/bad.sh:5:34: warning: Declare and assign separately to avoid masking return values. [SC2155]
(exit status 1; a clean script exits 0)

extra_findings.fact: With a #!/bin/sh shebang ShellCheck flags bashisms (SC3xxx series).
extra_findings.quote:
/tmp/posix.sh:2:3: warning: In POSIX sh, arrays are undefined. [SC3030]
/tmp/posix.sh:3:1: warning: In POSIX sh, [[ ]] is undefined. [SC3010]

teaching_notes: The four SC codes map one-to-one onto bash-manual facts (word splitting, set -e's blind spots, masked exit status), so they make good 'a tool will tell you' callouts. Useful nuance: SC2086 is only 'info' severity, and SC2164 switches itself off when the script contains set -e even though the wiki admits set -e 'won't necessarily prevent the issue'. SC2115 (rm -rf "$var"/*) fires alongside SC2086 and is the better hook for the 'agent deleted the box' story.
